claims.claim: Agent-driven repository, branch, PR and CI volume increases coordination pressure.
Git packfile/local-filesystem semantics make naive remote/distributed storage difficult.
Synchronous multi-replica ref transactions suffer tail-latency and replica-floor scalability limits.
A push should not be acknowledged before durable authoritative persistence.
Ref publication should be atomic/CAS-bound and operation history should be linearizable under the declared model.
Serving repositories may be disposable caches only when authoritative freshness and rebuild are verified.
Gossip may optimize propagation but must not be correctness authority.
Primary-only compaction can trade bandwidth for reduced per-replica CPU work.
Operation history can support corruption/race diagnosis, replay and recovery.
Read scaling and push-throughput numbers require exact topology, workload, durability, consistency and failure denominators.
